container: The gig economy describes a labor market where people earn income through short term jobs, freelance projects, or app based services instead of relying on permanent employment. Drivers, designers, tutors, and delivery workers may choose when and how much they work. This flexibility can support personal goals and provide extra income, but it also brings uncertainty. Many gig workers lack paid leave, health insurance, and predictable earnings. Understanding the gig economy means considering both convenience and risk. Governments, companies, and workers continue debating fair pay, safety, benefits, and protections for people whose livelihoods depend on temporary work.
